      "id": "c:4216096603",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "changing -bind semantics breaks setups that listen on one IP but load balance outbound connections",
      "quote": "This might break a scenario where someone wants to listen on one IP, but load balance outgoing connections. A new option might be better?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author implemented -outboundbind as a separate option",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4216582478",
        "c:4319952452",
        "c:4524241991"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:4524241991",
      "status_by_quote": "Added `-outboundbind=<addr>` as a separate option instead of extending `-bind`"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3078245893",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "add a comment clarifying that IsLocal() matches 0.0.0.0/8 and not just loopback",
      "quote": "Worth a comment somewhere, clarifying that?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author removed the special-casing and updated validation",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793779753"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3793779753",
      "status_by_quote": "Removed entirely. Addresses are used as given, then validated: parse, wildcard, and family checks, plus a trial `bind()` at init."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3078339596",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "storing the address without early validation silently kills outbound connections rather than failing loudly at startup",
      "quote": "misconfigured address fails loudly at init rather than silently killing outbound for that family",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added trial bind check at startup via IsAddrBindable()",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793780005"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3793780005",
      "status_by_quote": "Done. `IsAddrBindable()` does a trial `bind()` at init, so a misconfigured address fails startup."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3079619490",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "check that m_outbound_bind_v6 stays empty when an IPv4 address is stored",
      "quote": "You can avoid this by including `BOOST_CHECK(!connman->GetOutboundBindV6());` around here.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "assertion included in outbound_bind_address_selection unit test",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5311661451",
      "status_by_quote": "tests: ... unit (per-family selection and nothing for Tor/I2P/CJDNS"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3079687724",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "add a unit test calling ConnectDirectly with a bind address to verify the bind path",
      "quote": "add a unit test that calls `ConnectDirectly` with a bind address, even if just to verify the syscall is attempted",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added test verifying ConnectDirectly binds before connecting",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793780572"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3793780572",
      "status_by_quote": "Done. A unit test checks that `ConnectDirectly()` binds to the given source before connecting (recording mock socket via `CreateSock`), doesn't bind without one, and aborts on a failed bind."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:4317621161",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "binding outbound connections via -bind prevents the node from connecting to peers on the local LAN or VM bridge interfaces",
      "quote": "as proposed here -bind=mypublicinterface would suddenly make my node unable to connect to stuff on my local lan (or, in VM on bridge interfaces)-- pretty surprising.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author left -bind semantics untouched and introduced -outboundbind",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4319952452",
        "c:4524241991"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:4524241991",
      "status_by_quote": "Kept `-bind` semantics unchanged, so existing setups (including LAN/bridge peers) are unaffected"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3380951884",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "use 'address' rather than 'host' in the help description to avoid confusion with hostnames",
      "quote": "Better use \"address\" as \"host\" could be mistaken for a hostname.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author updated help text to specify bare address",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793780883"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3793780883",
      "status_by_quote": "Done. The help now says to give a bare address without a port"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3380992855",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "allowing port numbers in -outboundbind causes confusion since outgoing source ports should not be specified",
      "quote": "this will allow ports to be included, e.g. `-outboundbind=1.2.4.5:5678` which better not be allowed to avoid confusion.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author switched to LookupHost to reject ports at startup",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793780883",
        "rc:3793781233"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3793781233",
      "status_by_quote": "switched to `LookupHost()` so a port is rejected at startup."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3381078759",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "use CNetAddr instead of CService to store outbound bind addresses",
      "quote": "s/CService/CNetAddr/",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author stored CNetAddr instead of CService",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793781797"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3793781797",
      "status_by_quote": "Done, and replaced the vector with one `std::optional<CNetAddr>` per family."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3381134818",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "silently swallowing unusable addresses masks configuration errors",
      "quote": "What's the reason to silently swallow such addresses? It would be more obvious if we return an error for those at startup, like we do for invalid values.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added startup errors for unusable addresses",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793782102"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3793782102",
      "status_by_quote": "Nothing is dropped silently."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3381150540",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "allow -outboundbind=0.0.0.0 to clear earlier settings",
      "quote": "It might be desirable to use `-outboundbind=0.0.0.0` to remove the effect of a preceding `-outboundbind=...`.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained 0.0.0.0 is rejected and -nooutboundbind is provided instead",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793782439"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3793782439",
      "status_by_quote": "Use `-nooutboundbind` to clear an earlier setting."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3387230394",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "replace the vector of addresses with two std::optional<CNetAddr> members",
      "quote": "replace this vector with two `std::optional<CNetAddr>` members",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author implemented std::optional<CNetAddr> per family",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793781797"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3793781797",
      "status_by_quote": "Done, and replaced the vector with one `std::optional<CNetAddr>` per family."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3387250516",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "first-wins prevents overriding earlier configuration settings",
      "quote": "Usually the notion is that the last one wins. E.g. `-outboundbind=1.2.3.4 -outboundbind=5.6.7.8` -- `5.6.7.8` should be used. This helps override earlier settings which might be out of one's control.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained first-wins aligns with config file reverse precedence and asked if ArgsManager accessor is needed",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793783043"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3793783043",
      "status_by_quote": "first-wins matches the config-file convention (\"the first one is generally chosen\", doc/bitcoin-conf.md; reverse_precede"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3388680247",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "drop the unit test block that does not test the new feature",
      "quote": "This is not testing the new feature. Better drop it.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author replaced it with a direct test of address selection",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3793784224"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3793784224",
      "status_by_quote": "replaced it with a direct test of the feature"
    },

      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "use 1.1.1.5 and 1111:1111::5 provided by CI and keep functional test instructions consistent",
      "quote": "Recently the CI was extended to provide `1.1.1.5` and `1111:1111::5` on the VMs it creates to facilitate such tests.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author updated functional test to use CI-provided IPs",

        "rc:3793784537"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],

      "status_by_id": "rc:3793784537",
      "status_by_quote": "Done. The test binds `1.1.1.5`/`1111:1111::5` as the outgoing sources"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4537828536",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "add a functional test verifying that -nooutboundbind on the command line overrides a config-file outboundbind",

      "clears_with": "answer",

      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4541421010",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "clarify release notes by stating IPv4 and IPv6 can be configured independently, using 'local source address', and documenting -proxy behavior",
      "quote": "saying that one IPv4 and one IPv6 address can be configured independently makes it clearer what the option actually supports",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],

      "kind": "interface",

      "type": "question",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "ask whether adding a bool* out-parameter for bind_failed in ConnectDirectly is acceptable or if returning a failure reason alongside the socket is preferred",
      "quote": "is adding another out-param here fine, given the existing pattern, or would returning the failure reason alongside the socket be preferable ?",
      "clears_with": "answer",

      "text": "mention in the PR description that feature_bind_outgoing.py requires 1.1.1.5 and 1111:1111::5 on a non-loopback interface",

      "id": "rc:4579433374",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "deduplicate SockRestore into a shared SockFixture across unit test cases",
      "quote": "a shared fixture defines it once, so future `CreateSock` mocks reuse it instead of copy-pasting, and it still restores on a throwing `BOOST_REQUIRE`",

      "kind": "approach",

      "status": "open",

      "author_replies": [],

participants.note: objected to altering -bind semantics for outbound traffic as it could break load balancing
Concept ACK; suggested trial bind at startup and additional unit tests
objected to overloading -bind because it breaks local LAN and VM bridge peer connections
Concept ACK and Approach ACK; provided review feedback on validation, parsing, and tests
asked whether the author was still working on rebasing and addressing open reviews
Approach ACK; suggested -nooutboundbind test, release notes improvements, -onlynet warning, ClearnetSource type, and test fixture refactoring

claims.text: changing -bind semantics breaks setups that listen on one IP but load balance outbound connections
claims.quote: This might break a scenario where someone wants to listen on one IP, but load balance outgoing connections. A new option might be better?
claims.status_note: author implemented -outboundbind as a separate option
claims.status_by_quote: Added `-outboundbind=<addr>` as a separate option instead of extending `-bind`

claims.text: add a comment clarifying that IsLocal() matches 0.0.0.0/8 and not just loopback
claims.quote: Worth a comment somewhere, clarifying that?
claims.status_note: author removed the special-casing and updated validation
claims.status_by_quote: Removed entirely. Addresses are used as given, then validated: parse, wildcard, and family checks, plus a trial `bind()` at init.

claims.text: storing the address without early validation silently kills outbound connections rather than failing loudly at startup
claims.quote: misconfigured address fails loudly at init rather than silently killing outbound for that family
claims.status_note: author added trial bind check at startup via IsAddrBindable()
claims.status_by_quote: Done. `IsAddrBindable()` does a trial `bind()` at init, so a misconfigured address fails startup.

claims.text: check that m_outbound_bind_v6 stays empty when an IPv4 address is stored
claims.quote: You can avoid this by including `BOOST_CHECK(!connman->GetOutboundBindV6());` around here.
claims.status_note: assertion included in outbound_bind_address_selection unit test
claims.status_by_quote: tests: ... unit (per-family selection and nothing for Tor/I2P/CJDNS

claims.text: add a unit test calling ConnectDirectly with a bind address to verify the bind path
claims.quote: add a unit test that calls `ConnectDirectly` with a bind address, even if just to verify the syscall is attempted
claims.status_note: author added test verifying ConnectDirectly binds before connecting
claims.status_by_quote: Done. A unit test checks that `ConnectDirectly()` binds to the given source before connecting (recording mock socket via `CreateSock`), doesn't bind without one, and aborts on a failed bind.

claims.text: binding outbound connections via -bind prevents the node from connecting to peers on the local LAN or VM bridge interfaces
claims.quote: as proposed here -bind=mypublicinterface would suddenly make my node unable to connect to stuff on my local lan (or, in VM on bridge interfaces)-- pretty surprising.
claims.status_note: author left -bind semantics untouched and introduced -outboundbind
claims.status_by_quote: Kept `-bind` semantics unchanged, so existing setups (including LAN/bridge peers) are unaffected

claims.text: use 'address' rather than 'host' in the help description to avoid confusion with hostnames
claims.quote: Better use "address" as "host" could be mistaken for a hostname.
claims.status_note: author updated help text to specify bare address
claims.status_by_quote: Done. The help now says to give a bare address without a port

claims.text: allowing port numbers in -outboundbind causes confusion since outgoing source ports should not be specified
claims.quote: this will allow ports to be included, e.g. `-outboundbind=1.2.4.5:5678` which better not be allowed to avoid confusion.
claims.status_note: author switched to LookupHost to reject ports at startup
claims.status_by_quote: switched to `LookupHost()` so a port is rejected at startup.

claims.text: use CNetAddr instead of CService to store outbound bind addresses
claims.quote: s/CService/CNetAddr/
claims.status_note: author stored CNetAddr instead of CService
claims.status_by_quote: Done, and replaced the vector with one `std::optional<CNetAddr>` per family.

claims.text: silently swallowing unusable addresses masks configuration errors
claims.quote: What's the reason to silently swallow such addresses? It would be more obvious if we return an error for those at startup, like we do for invalid values.
claims.status_note: author added startup errors for unusable addresses

claims.text: allow -outboundbind=0.0.0.0 to clear earlier settings
claims.quote: It might be desirable to use `-outboundbind=0.0.0.0` to remove the effect of a preceding `-outboundbind=...`.
claims.status_note: author explained 0.0.0.0 is rejected and -nooutboundbind is provided instead
claims.status_by_quote: Use `-nooutboundbind` to clear an earlier setting.

claims.text: replace the vector of addresses with two std::optional<CNetAddr> members
claims.quote: replace this vector with two `std::optional<CNetAddr>` members
claims.status_by_quote: Done, and replaced the vector with one `std::optional<CNetAddr>` per family.

claims.text: first-wins prevents overriding earlier configuration settings
claims.quote: Usually the notion is that the last one wins. E.g. `-outboundbind=1.2.3.4 -outboundbind=5.6.7.8` -- `5.6.7.8` should be used. This helps override earlier settings which might be out of one's control.
claims.status_note: author explained first-wins aligns with config file reverse precedence and asked if ArgsManager accessor is needed
claims.status_by_quote: first-wins matches the config-file convention ("the first one is generally chosen", doc/bitcoin-conf.md; reverse_precede

claims.text: drop the unit test block that does not test the new feature
claims.quote: This is not testing the new feature. Better drop it.
claims.status_note: author replaced it with a direct test of address selection
claims.status_by_quote: replaced it with a direct test of the feature

claims.text: use 1.1.1.5 and 1111:1111::5 provided by CI and keep functional test instructions consistent
claims.quote: Recently the CI was extended to provide `1.1.1.5` and `1111:1111::5` on the VMs it creates to facilitate such tests.
claims.status_note: author updated functional test to use CI-provided IPs
claims.status_by_quote: Done. The test binds `1.1.1.5`/`1111:1111::5` as the outgoing sources

claims.text: add a functional test verifying that -nooutboundbind on the command line overrides a config-file outboundbind
claims.quote: could we add a functional test with `outboundbind=<addr>` in the config file and `-nooutboundbind` on the command line, asserting that the outgoing source is no longer the address in the configuration file ?

claims.text: clarify release notes by stating IPv4 and IPv6 can be configured independently, using 'local source address', and documenting -proxy behavior
claims.quote: saying that one IPv4 and one IPv6 address can be configured independently makes it clearer what the option actually supports

claims.text: add an InitWarning when -outboundbind is set for an address family excluded by -onlynet
claims.quote: could we add a similar warning when `-outboundbind` is set for a family excluded by `-onlynet`.. with a functional test covering the warning, if necessary ?

claims.text: ask whether adding a bool* out-parameter for bind_failed in ConnectDirectly is acceptable or if returning a failure reason alongside the socket is preferred
claims.quote: is adding another out-param here fine, given the existing pattern, or would returning the failure reason alongside the socket be preferable ?

claims.text: mention in the PR description that feature_bind_outgoing.py requires 1.1.1.5 and 1111:1111::5 on a non-loopback interface
claims.quote: could the PR description mention that `feature_bind_outgoing.py` needs `1.1.1.5` and `1111:1111::5` assigned to a non-loopback interface (CI sets them already), and that it skips otherwise ?

claims.text: deduplicate SockRestore into a shared SockFixture across unit test cases
claims.quote: a shared fixture defines it once, so future `CreateSock` mocks reuse it instead of copy-pasting, and it still restores on a throwing `BOOST_REQUIRE`

claims.text: introduce a dedicated ClearnetSource type representing only specific IPv4 or IPv6 addresses to enforce clearnet source invariants by type
claims.quote: introduce a _dedicated type_ that can only represent a specific IPv4 or IPv6 address

support.reason: I agree that it is better to not change the semantic of the existent `-bind` and introduce a new option instead with a default value "leave it to the OS" which is the same as of before this PR.
